messages.subject: Permutation for Distant / Trans Associations
parts:
Hi I was wondering if the permutation statistic can also be applied for distant / trans associations. Many researchers have told me that distant effects require more stringent LOD cutoffs. I was wondering if there is a means to empirically derive this? I am working with the DO mouse line.

Thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Permutation for Distant / Trans Associations
parts:
The typical permutation approach is adjusting for the scan across the genome but only considering a single trait. You could use a similar approach to control the family-wise error rate in the search across both the genome and across multiple phenotypes. Alternatively, you could control the family-wise error rate for the genome scan of a phenotype, but then control the false discovery rate in the search across phenotypes, for example with the qvalue package.

karl
